solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Horse flies back with letter for Homer (7)

indicatorNotes.back: 'back' as in going back the way you came, so the flies are written in reverse

blocks.note: mu is a Greek letter, the alphabet Homer wrote in

annotation.surface: A horse is plagued by flies, and someone reaches for a line of Homer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flies' reads as a verb, the horse flying back; it is a plural noun for insects. 'Homer' is the Greek poet, not the Simpson.
annotation.definitionFit: A mustang is a wild horse of the American plains, so it is a plain synonym by example.

entries.clue: Old Italian family hotel in orderly city (8,3)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' says the hotel is located inside the word for orderly

blocks.note: the Medici, rulers of Renaissance Florence
H is hotel in the NATO alphabet
neat = orderly; H goes inside it

annotation.surface: A historic Italian dynasty runs a hotel in a well-kept city.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue's Italian flavour points away from the Canadian prairies, where this city is.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Medicine Hat is a small city in Alberta, Canada, named after a Blackfoot legend.

entries.clue: Film River without river (5)

indicatorNotes.without: 'without' means lacking, so the river's name must go without its R

annotation.surface: A title card: the film called River, but with no actual river in it.
annotation.walkthrough: The Severn flows through Wales and western England. 'Film River' looks like a movie title, which hides that River is a real river to name.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Seven is David Fincher's 1995 serial-killer thriller.

entries.clue: Drink six-pack wearing short article (7)

indicatorNotes.short: 'short' means lacking a bit at the end, so the article loses its last letter

blocks.note: a six-pack is a set of well-defined abdominal muscles
wearing = in, as in 'in a hat'
the definite article THE, cut short

annotation.surface: Someone orders a drink while showing off their abs in a skimpy item of clothing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Six-pack' and 'Drink' together suggest beer cans; the six-pack is the stomach muscles instead. ABSINTH is an accepted spelling of absinthe.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym by example: absinth is a strong anise-flavoured spirit, a drink.

entries.clue: Horrid row with expert over channel’s economic indicator? (5,8,7)

blocks.note: a domestic is a household quarrel

annotation.surface: A nasty argument breaks out with an expert about some channel's economic figures.
annotation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'over' places the first parts above the channel. A 'domestic' as a noun is British slang for a row at home, often one the police are called to.
annotation.definitionFit: GDP, the total value of what a country produces, is the headline measure economists watch.

entries.clue: Fifty maybe touching base in interval (8)

indicatorNotes.touching: 'touching' means in contact with, so the base sits right up against the fifty

blocks.note: a ton is a hundred, so half a ton, a semi-ton, is fifty
e is the base of natural logarithms

annotation.surface: A batsman on fifty, touching base during a break in play.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ton' is British slang for a hundred (runs, pounds, miles per hour). 'Interval' reads as a break; here it is the musical kind.
annotation.definitionFit: In music an interval is the gap between two notes, and a semitone is the smallest one.

entries.clue: Exhibit part of production? (9)

blocks.note: a noun: the prize item put on display
a production is a show, and a part of it is a piece

annotation.surface: A museum label wondering whether an exhibit came from a stage production.
annotation.walkthrough: The second definition is whimsical, hence the question mark: split SHOWPIECE into SHOW and PIECE.
annotation.definitionFit: A showpiece is the star exhibit; read in two words it is literally a piece of a show.

entries.clue: Mate gutted fish around Donnybrook (5)

indicatorNotes.gutted: a gutted fish has its insides removed, so MATE loses its middle
indicatorNotes.around: 'around' as in turned around, so the fish faces the other way

blocks.note: MATE with its middle letters AT removed

annotation.surface: A shipmate cleans fish somewhere around an Irish place.
annotation.walkthrough: Donnybrook, a Dublin district once famous for a riotous fair, gives its name to any brawl; 'around' makes it look like geography.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a donnybrook is a free-for-all fight, and so is a mêlée.

entries.clue: White crystals fleets regularly found between keys (5,4)

indicatorNotes.regularly: 'regularly' means at regular intervals, so take every other letter
indicatorNotes.found between: 'between' places those letters in the gap between the two keys

blocks.note: the Tab key on a keyboard

annotation.surface: Salt-white crystals turn up among the keys on a ship's fleet.
annotation.walkthrough: One plural word supplies both outer pieces, one key on each side. 'Keys' also evokes low islands, which suits the fleets.
annotation.definitionFit: Table salt is sodium chloride, sold as fine white crystals.

entries.clue: Reformed Lutheran releasing husband without charge (7)

indicatorNotes.Reformed: 're-formed' means given a new form, so the letters are rearranged
indicatorNotes.releasing: 'releasing' means letting go of, so H leaves the fodder

blocks.note: the fodder before H is dropped

annotation.surface: A Lutheran who has converted lets a husband off without a fee.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Reformed' sits naturally beside a Protestant, but it means rearranged. 'Charge' is electrical, not a fee.
annotation.definitionFit: In physics a neutral particle carries no electric charge.

entries.clue: Mushroom jelly mainly frozen (6)

indicatorNotes.mainly: 'mainly' means for the most part, so take most of the word and drop its last letter

blocks.note: agar is a jelly made from seaweed

annotation.surface: A dessert of mushroom jelly, mostly still frozen.
annotation.walkthrough: Agar is the gel used in laboratory dishes and vegetarian jellies.
annotation.definitionFit: Agaric is the botanical name for gilled mushrooms such as the fly agaric.

entries.clue: European country reduced by half? This means nothing to American state (7)

indicatorNotes.reduced by half?: cut to half its size, so only three of GREECE's six letters survive

blocks.note: GREECE cut to its first half
nada is American slang for nothing

annotation.surface: A shrinking European country, and a word meaning nothing to an American state.
annotation.walkthrough: 'American state' looks like one phrase; 'to American' belongs to NADA, and 'state' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: State in the sense of sovereign nation: Grenada is an island nation in the Caribbean.

entries.clue: Doris dancing with chap in ecstasy (9)

indicatorNotes.dancing: dancers never stay in one place, so the letters move into a new order

annotation.surface: Doris is dancing with a man and loving every minute.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a happy scene that is also a hint at the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Rhapsodic means wildly enthusiastic, the state of someone in ecstasy.

entries.clue: Horse first crossing large single paving unit? (11)

indicatorNotes.crossing: to cross something is to go across it, so BEST spans L and holds it inside

blocks.note: a cob is a sturdy horse
L = large, as on clothes labels
first = best; L goes after its B

annotation.surface: A horse is first to cross a big stone slab.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the 'unit' is one stone among many in a paved road.
annotation.definitionFit: Cobblestones are rounded stones laid one by one to pave a street, so each is a unit of paving.

entries.clue: This method of production could make our lab? (8,2,6)

annotation.definition: This method of production could make our lab?

blocks.note: the straight reading: an economic way of organising work
the joke: divide up the word LABOUR and its letters can make OUR LAB

annotation.surface: A plan to reorganise production to build a laboratory for us.
annotation.walkthrough: The phrase names the economic practice of splitting work into specialised tasks, and taken literally, a division of LABOUR rearranges it into OUR LAB.
annotation.definitionFit: Adam Smith's pin factory is the classic example of division of labour as a method of production.

entries.clue: Smear base of flower with a tube’s contents (6)

indicatorNotes.contents: a tube's contents are what is inside it, so take the middle letters

blocks.note: a flower bed is where flowers are based

annotation.surface: Instructions to smear the bottom of a flower with something squeezed from a tube.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Base of flower' suggests the stem, or the last letter R; it is a flower bed.
annotation.definitionFit: To bedaub is to smear something all over, usually messily.

entries.clue: Drunk dentist who’s struggling with teeth here (5,6,2,3,4)

indicatorNotes.struggling: something struggling is thrashing about, so the letters are in disarray

annotation.surface: A tipsy dentist fumbling with a patient's teeth.
annotation.walkthrough: The drunk dentist is a real picture, and 'Drunk' is also the definition. The phrase comes from sailing: a sail whose sheets (ropes) are loose flaps about.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom: three sheets to the wind means very drunk, staggering like a badly rigged sailing ship.

entries.clue: Priest Yankee lifted from gorge (5)

indicatorNotes.lifted from: to lift something from a place is to take it away, so Y is removed

blocks.note: Y is Yankee in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: A priest and an American are hauled up out of a ravine.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Yankee' looks like a person being rescued; it is the radio code word for Y.
annotation.definitionFit: In Anglican churches a canon is a priest attached to a cathedral.

entries.clue: Chief canal nearly jammed by early arrival (7)

indicatorNotes.nearly: 'nearly' means not quite all, so drop the canal's last letter
indicatorNotes.jammed by: a jammed canal has something stuck in it, so the early arrival goes inside

blocks.note: a prem is a premature baby

annotation.surface: The main canal is blocked by a ship that turned up early.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Prem' is everyday British hospital slang for a premature baby, and 'early arrival' disguises it as a ship.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: chief and supreme both mean highest in rank.

entries.clue: Practice of judges welcomed by Brazilian capital (9)

indicatorNotes.welcomed by: to be welcomed is to be taken in, so the judges go inside the capital

annotation.surface: Judges' custom of being received in Brasília.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Brazilian capital' asks for a city; it is capital in the money sense.
annotation.definitionFit: A rehearsal is a practice run before the real performance.

entries.clue: Help Ron to cast Frozen part (5,4)

indicatorNotes.cast: to cast is to throw, and letters thrown land in a new order

annotation.surface: A request to help Ron get cast in a part in the film Frozen.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Frozen' capitalised, with 'cast' and 'part', paints a movie audition; the part is a part of the globe.
annotation.definitionFit: The North Pole is the ice-covered top of the Earth, a frozen part of the planet.

entries.clue: Fickle motorist avoiding motorway food in Italy (7)

indicatorNotes.Fickle: fickle means changeable, so the letters change their order
indicatorNotes.avoiding: to avoid something is to keep it out, so M is left out

blocks.note: M is the prefix of British motorways, like the M1

annotation.surface: A capricious driver skips the motorway services on a food tour of Italy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fickle' sits at the front, far from the word it works on, and reads as a description of the driver.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: risotto is a creamy northern Italian rice dish.

entries.clue: Fool cleaner with story (7)

blocks.note: a char, or charwoman, is an old word for a cleaning lady

annotation.surface: A gullible cleaner who spins a yarn.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Story' sounds like a tale told; it is a fib, as in 'don't tell stories'.
annotation.definitionFit: British slang: to feel 'a right charlie' is to feel a fool.

entries.clue: Football team from Sussex town throwing away win (7)

indicatorNotes.throwing away: to throw something away is to discard it, so WIN is dropped

blocks.note: Winchelsea is a small town in East Sussex

annotation.surface: A Sussex side is throwing away a victory, as football teams do.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a match report about a lost lead, which hides that 'win' is literal letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Chelsea FC is a London Premier League football club.

entries.clue: Range of cell components with nothing missing (5)

indicatorNotes.missing: something missing is absent, so O is taken out

blocks.note: an electric cell (battery) has anodes as components

annotation.surface: A range of parts for cells, none of them missing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cell' suggests biology; it is a battery cell.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the Andes are the mountain range along South America's west coast.

entries.clue: Religious adherent eats fish (5)

blocks.note: to have a meal = to eat it
the id, or ide, is a freshwater fish

annotation.surface: A devout believer eats fish.
annotation.walkthrough: The ID (ide) is a crossword staple fish, a European carp.
annotation.definitionFit: A Hasid follows Hasidism, a strictly observant Jewish movement.

entries.clue: See fashion designer cut short notices to audience (7)

indicatorNotes.cut short: cutting something short trims its end, so Dior loses its last letter
indicatorNotes.to audience: said to an audience, so what matters is the sound, not the spelling

annotation.surface: Go and look at a fashion designer who is abruptly handing out announcements to a crowd.
annotation.walkthrough: 'See' opens the clue looking like a command; it is a noun, a bishop's area of authority.
annotation.definitionFit: A bishop's see is the district he governs, which is his diocese.

entries.clue: Some clientele — men — talked about the weather? (9)

indicatorNotes.Some: 'some' means a portion of, so the answer is part of the words that follow

annotation.surface: Some of the customers, all men, made small talk about the weather.
annotation.walkthrough: The dashes break up the run of letters, but hidden answers leap punctuation. The question mark flags a stretched definition.
annotation.definitionFit: The elements can mean wind and rain, so elemental can mean concerning the weather.

entries.clue: Landowner’s daughter introduced by Den (5)

indicatorNotes.introduced by: someone introduced by another comes after them, so the daughter follows Den

blocks.note: a den is an animal's lair

annotation.surface: A landowner's daughter is presented to society by someone called Den.
annotation.walkthrough: '’s' stands for 'is'. Den looks like a man's name; it is a lair.
annotation.definitionFit: Regional use: laird is the Scottish word for a landed proprietor.

entries.clue: It blows knight against officer on exposed rock (7)

indicatorNotes.against: 'against' as in leaning against, so the rest sits right next to the knight
indicatorNotes.on: in an across answer, one thing on another comes after it
indicatorNotes.exposed: something exposed has lost its cover, so ROCK loses its outer letters

blocks.note: rOCk with its covering letters stripped

annotation.surface: A knight squares up to an officer on a bare rock, and something blows.
annotation.walkthrough: The rock goes before the officer because 'on' means after in an across answer. 'It blows' sounds like an exclamation, but it defines a wind.
annotation.definitionFit: The sirocco is a hot wind from North Africa, something that blows.

entries.clue: Once again fixes damaged NHS gear (7)

indicatorNotes.damaged: damaged goods are knocked out of shape, so the letters are knocked out of order

annotation.surface: Someone repairs hospital equipment yet again.
annotation.walkthrough: The NHS is Britain's National Health Service; 'fixes' reads as repairs but means fastens up, as a picture on a wall.
annotation.definitionFit: To hang a picture is to fix it in place, so rehanging fixes it once again.

entries.clue: Keep blocking Thirty Acts periodically in retribution (3,3,3)

indicatorNotes.blocking: something blocking a path sits in the middle of it, so the keep goes inside
indicatorNotes.periodically: 'periodically' means at regular intervals, so take every other letter

blocks.note: a keep is a castle's stronghold
the 1st, 3rd, 5th, 7th and 9th letters of THIRTY ACTS

annotation.surface: Keep blocking thirty acts from time to time as revenge.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Keep' opens as an instruction; it is a noun, the strongest tower of a castle.
annotation.definitionFit: Tit for tat is retaliation in kind, a blow for a blow.

entries.clue: Swimmer getting shot of last fast car (5)

indicatorNotes.getting shot of last: 'getting shot of' is British for getting rid of, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: a turbot is a flatfish; 'swimmer' = fish

annotation.surface: A swimmer, shot at last, and a fast car: an action film.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Swimmer' suggests a person; in crosswords it is often a fish.
annotation.definitionFit: A turbo is short for a turbocharged car, built for speed.

entries.clue: Tip from raid following action in court (7,6)

indicatorNotes.following: to follow is to come after, so the raid comes after the court action

blocks.note: a service is a shot on a tennis court

annotation.surface: A tip-off from a police raid that followed a court case.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Action in court' reads as a lawsuit; the court is a tennis court.
annotation.definitionFit: A service charge is a tip added automatically to a restaurant bill.

entries.clue: Most foul tirade about Loach’s work (7)

indicatorNotes.about: 'about' as in surrounding, so the rant goes round the film

blocks.note: Kes is Ken Loach's 1969 film about a boy and a kestrel

annotation.surface: A foul-mouthed rant about a Ken Loach film.
annotation.walkthrough: Ken Loach is a British director of gritty social dramas; Kes is his best-known film.
annotation.definitionFit: Rank means foul-smelling or gross, so rankest is the superlative.

entries.clue: Spinning plant stores popular wine (7)

indicatorNotes.Spinning: something spinning turns round, so the plant is written backwards
indicatorNotes.stores: to store something is to keep it inside, so the turned plant holds IN

annotation.surface: A spinning mill's shop sells a popular wine.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plant' and 'stores' suggest a factory and its shops, not a flower holding a word.
annotation.definitionFit: Retsina is a Greek white wine flavoured with pine resin.

entries.clue: You might draw this nude beneath a rose? (6,7)

annotation.definition: You might draw this nude beneath a rose?

blocks.note: draw as in pull across, not sketch
a rose is the perforated head of a shower, and you stand naked under it

annotation.surface: An artist sketches a nude model posed beneath a rose.
annotation.walkthrough: The art-class picture hides a bathroom: you pull this across while standing naked under the shower.
annotation.definitionFit: A shower curtain is drawn closed by someone showering, naked under the rose.

entries.clue: Acrobatic moves of seasonal crew reported? (11)

indicatorNotes.reported: a report is spoken aloud, so go by the sound of the words

blocks.note: summer = seasonal; salts = sailors, a crew

annotation.surface: The tumbling routines of a crew hired for the summer.
annotation.walkthrough: An old salt is a veteran sailor, so salts make up a crew.
annotation.definitionFit: Somersaults are head-over-heels flips, staple acrobatic moves.

entries.clue: Set off from school patrolled by fuddy-duddy (9)

indicatorNotes.patrolled by: a patrol goes all round an area, so DATED goes round the school

annotation.surface: Someone leaves a school watched over by a stuffy old teacher.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Set off' looks like departing; it means exploded. Eton is a famous English boarding school.
annotation.definitionFit: Phrasal-verb synonym: triggering an explosive charge is both setting it off and detonating it.

entries.clue: Bash the German character outside local yard (6,5)

indicatorNotes.outside: 'outside' means on the outer side, so DER wraps round the local

blocks.note: your local is your nearby pub
a character in a play is a part

annotation.surface: A German character beats someone up outside the pub.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bash' opens like a violent verb; it is informal British for a party. 'Local' is British for the neighbourhood pub.
annotation.definitionFit: Informal British: a bash is a party, and a dinner party is one kind.

entries.clue: Wrongly pick up female at this place in auditorium (7)

indicatorNotes.in auditorium: an auditorium is where things are heard, so go by the sound

blocks.note: Ms (said 'miz') = a female title; here = at this place

annotation.surface: A man fails to chat up a woman in a theatre.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pick up' suggests a romantic approach; it means catch by ear.
annotation.definitionFit: Informal sense: 'pick up' can mean catch a sound, and the prefix MIS- supplies 'wrongly'.

entries.clue: Spend a lot climbing mountains on Yell (6,3)

indicatorNotes.climbing: in a down answer, climbing means going upwards, so the word reads from the bottom

annotation.surface: Paying a fortune to go mountain climbing on Yell.
annotation.walkthrough: Yell is one of the Shetland Islands, so the capital letter makes it look like a place; here it is simply a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: British idiom: the image is of money splashed about freely, as on a treat or luxury.

entries.clue: Performing actor books there and then (2-3-4)

blocks.note: OT = the Old Testament, a set of books

annotation.surface: An actor on stage books a job immediately.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Books' looks like a verb; it is a noun, the Old Testament's books.
annotation.definitionFit: An on-the-spot fine is given there and then, immediately.

entries.clue: Those people record rescue vessel in attraction (5,4)

blocks.note: an EP is an extended-play record

annotation.surface: People recording a rescue boat at a tourist attraction.
annotation.walkthrough: 'in' joins the wordplay to the definition, and makes the attraction sound like a location.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a theme park is a tourist attraction built round rides.

entries.clue: Voracious fish caught unfortunate dog (9)

indicatorNotes.caught: as in 'I didn't catch what you said', catching a word means hearing it

blocks.note: poor = unfortunate; a beagle is a dog

annotation.surface: A hungry fish catches an unlucky dog.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Caught' reads as the fish's attack but means heard.
annotation.definitionFit: The porbeagle is a mackerel shark, a large and hungry predator.

entries.clue: Young family member caught one boring issue (5)

indicatorNotes.boring: to bore is to drill into, so C and I tunnel inside the issue

annotation.surface: A youngster in the family caught up in one dull matter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Boring' and 'issue' look like a tedious topic; boring means piercing and issue means offspring.
annotation.definitionFit: A scion is a descendant, especially a young member of a notable family.

entries.clue: Church boxing up priest’s souvenir (5)

indicatorNotes.boxing up: to box something up is to enclose it, so RC goes round the priest

blocks.note: Eli, the priest in the Book of Samuel

annotation.surface: A church packing up a priest's keepsake.
annotation.walkthrough: '’s' stands for 'is'. Eli is the crossword's usual priest.
annotation.definitionFit: A relic is an object kept in memory of the past, much as a souvenir is.

entries.clue: Two types of preserve primarily available in Mexican bar? (7)

indicatorNotes.primarily: 'primarily' means first of all, so take the first letter

blocks.note: to can and to tin are both ways of preserving food

annotation.surface: A Mexican bar stocks two kinds of jam, mainly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Preserve' reads as jam; it is the verb, to preserve food in a can or tin.
annotation.definitionFit: Regional use: cantina is the Spanish word for a bar, used in Mexico and the American Southwest.

entries.clue: Most adroit adult leaves audiology appointment? (7)

indicatorNotes.leaves: one who leaves goes away, so A departs from the phrase

blocks.note: a deaf test, a hearing check

annotation.surface: The cleverest grown-up walks out of a hearing test.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark allows the made-up phrase 'deaf test' for a hearing test.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: deft means adroit, so deftest is most adroit.

entries.clue: Leaves aged person briefly interrupted by trouble from below (7)

indicatorNotes.briefly: said briefly, a word is cut short of its last letter
indicatorNotes.interrupted by: an interruption breaks into the middle, so the trouble goes inside
indicatorNotes.from below: in a down answer, coming from below means reading upwards

annotation.surface: An old person departs, cut short by trouble from beneath.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' opens looking like a verb, as if the fogey is walking out.
annotation.definitionFit: Foliage is the collective word for a plant's leaves.

entries.clue: Repay in kind network shielding exposed European (9)

indicatorNotes.shielding: to shield something is to surround and protect it, so the network wraps round
indicatorNotes.exposed: something exposed has lost its cover, so strip the outer letters

blocks.note: a rete is a network of nerves or vessels
ITALIAN with its outer letters stripped

annotation.surface: A network protecting a vulnerable European hits back.
annotation.walkthrough: Rete is an anatomical word for a mesh of blood vessels.
annotation.definitionFit: To retaliate is to pay someone back with the same treatment.

entries.clue: Film director hides old letter relating to Flower of Hades (7)

indicatorNotes.hides: to hide something is to keep it inside, so LEAN holds the letter

blocks.note: David Lean, director of Lawrence of Arabia
eth, the Old English letter ð

annotation.surface: A director keeps an old letter about the flowers of the underworld.
annotation.walkthrough: A 'flower' here is something that flows, a river: Lethe is the river of forgetfulness in Hades.
annotation.definitionFit: Crossword-only sense: a flower is a river, and Lethean means belonging to Lethe, the river of Hades.

entries.clue: Potentially toxic hulled rice fed to team (9)

indicatorNotes.hulled: hulled grain has its husk removed, so only the inside of RICE stays
indicatorNotes.fed to: food fed to someone ends up inside them, so IC goes into the team

annotation.surface: A team is given rice that may have been poisoned.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hulled' fits rice naturally; here it strips the word's outer letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Arsenical means containing arsenic, a classic poison.

entries.clue: Great old band in wings of theatre (7)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' places the band inside the other letters
indicatorNotes.wings of: a stage's wings are its two sides, so take the outer letters

annotation.surface: A great band of old playing in the wings of a theatre.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wings' is a real part of a theatre, which is what makes it hide so well.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: great and extreme both mean very large in degree.

entries.clue: Some northbound magi attacked in pine forest (5)

indicatorNotes.Some: 'some' means a portion of, so the answer lies within the next words
indicatorNotes.northbound: north is up on a map, so in a down answer the letters read upwards

annotation.surface: Some wise men heading north are ambushed in a forest.
annotation.walkthrough: The magi are the three wise men of the Nativity, whose journey makes 'northbound' look like travel.
annotation.definitionFit: The taiga is the vast coniferous forest of the far north, much of it pine.

entries.clue: It may be picked from empty utensil within dump (5)

indicatorNotes.empty: an empty container has nothing inside, so keep only the outer letters
indicatorNotes.within: 'within' means inside, so UL goes inside the dump

blocks.note: a tip is a rubbish dump

annotation.surface: Something you might pick out of an empty pot left at a rubbish dump.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tip' is British for a rubbish dump. 'It may be picked' fits any flower, which makes the definition vague on purpose.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: tulips are grown to be picked for bouquets.

entries.clue: President’s wife avoiding fine in car (5)

indicatorNotes.avoiding: to avoid something is to keep clear of it, so F is left out

blocks.note: FLOTUS = First Lady of the United States

annotation.surface: The First Lady dodges a fine while riding in a car.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fine' reads as a penalty; it is the pencil-grade abbreviation.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Lotus is a British maker of sports cars, and a Lotus is one of them.

entries.clue: Chance to succeed in game with relatives (4-2)

blocks.note: loo is an old card game

annotation.surface: A family trying to win a game against their relations.
annotation.walkthrough: Loo is a 17th-century card game, a crossword regular; in Britain it is also the toilet.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom: not getting a look-in means having no chance to take part or win.

entries.clue: Executive staff getting older police officer and cleric (8,8)

blocks.note: a rector is a parish priest

annotation.surface: An executive's staff are all ageing policemen and clergy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Staff' is a verb here, though the surface uses it as the noun for employees.
annotation.definitionFit: British usage: the managing director is the top executive running a company, the CEO.

entries.clue: Recalled role playing governor (6)

indicatorNotes.Recalled: to recall is to call back, so the words come back in reverse

annotation.surface: An actor remembers playing a governor's role.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Recalled' reads as remembered; it means called back.
annotation.definitionFit: A satrap was a provincial governor in ancient Persia.

entries.clue: Chain of drink locations originally superb (8)

indicatorNotes.originally: 'originally' means at the origin, the start, so take the first letter

blocks.note: to neck a drink is British slang for gulping it

annotation.surface: A chain of bars in great locations.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Chain of drink locations' reads as a pub chain, which hides that 'Chain' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a necklace is often a chain worn round the neck.
